text: Train the current user/video/request-context scorer with mixed-group ListNet top-one loss instead of within-user RankNet, emphasizing competition at the top of each intact candidate group.
rationale: Experiment 2 shows strong overall ordering but very poor top-five performance on several tabs, especially tab 8; a listwise objective directly targets top-of-group allocation rather than all positive-negative pairs equally.
exact_ablation: Change only the training loss from within-user RankNet pairwise loss to mixed-group ListNet top-one cross-entropy over complete mixed-label groups; retain the same features, model, optimizer, batch budget, split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, because listwise normalization may improve within-group ordering but can sacrifice some pairwise comparisons.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Modest positive change, approximately +0.001 to +0.008, if the top-five weakness reflects insufficient emphasis on the highest-ranked candidates.

text: Replace pairwise RankNet with user-normalized pointwise BCE so every displayed impression contributes while each complete user candidate group receives equal objective weight.
rationale: RankNet slightly reduced both official metrics relative to experiment 1, while the evaluation combines within-user ordering and macro top-five quality; equal group weighting offers a distinct low-variance objective that also retains homogeneous groups.
exact_ablation: Change only the loss from within-user RankNet to user-normalized BCE averaged within each complete user candidate group; retain current features, additive scorer, optimizer, sampling, split, and early stopping.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, if pairwise training is overfitting mixed groups or underusing homogeneous groups.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat or modest negative change, approximately -0.003 to +0.003, because pointwise BCE does not explicitly focus on the top five.

text: Replace the additive scorer with a compact embedding-plus-MLP ranker that can learn nonlinear interactions among user ID, video ID, and the already available impression context.
rationale: The request-context screen has positive primary lift, but the additive model can only add independent field effects; an interaction-capable scorer may personalize context effects to users and candidates, particularly where aggregate context performance is weak.
exact_ablation: Change only the scoring architecture from the additive linear logit to a small embedding-concatenation MLP over user ID, video ID, tab, hour, and weekday; retain pointwise BCE, optimizer, feature values, split, and sampling.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive change, approximately +0.001 to +0.006, if user-context and video-context interactions resolve within-user ordering errors.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive change, approximately 0 to +0.006, with upside concentrated in context segments where the additive context terms are insufficient.

text: Add a compact strictly causal recent-video sequence encoder to the current scorer, using only user events occurring before each impression.
rationale: The current model has no behavioral history and experiment 2 remains weak on top-five ordering; causal history can represent evolving intent that stable user/video additive terms cannot capture.
exact_ablation: Add only a capped causal recent-video history representation with a one-block sequence encoder and concatenate it with the existing scorer input; retain the current features, RankNet loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential moderate positive change, approximately 0 to +0.010, mainly for users with sufficient prior activity; sparse users may be unchanged.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential moderate positive change, approximately 0 to +0.012, if recent intent helps select the most relevant candidates near rank five.

text: Use candidate-conditioned attention over each user's strictly pre-impression recent-video history so different candidate videos activate different historical interests.
rationale: A fixed user representation cannot distinguish multiple interests; candidate-conditioned pooling is a materially different history mechanism and could improve the severe top-five weakness without using any post-impression signal.
exact_ablation: Add only a candidate-conditioned attention-pooled causal history vector to the existing scorer; retain current IDs, request context, RankNet loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential moderate positive change, approximately +0.001 to +0.012, especially for users with multiple positive candidates or heterogeneous histories.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential moderate positive change, approximately +0.002 to +0.015, because candidate-relative interest matching directly affects top-ranked candidates.

text: Add a single impression-time interaction between tab and hour rather than adding another broad feature family.
rationale: Request context is the only positively screened feature family, while tab 8 and tab 3 are the weakest validation slices; a tab-by-hour interaction tests whether context effects vary across surfaces and times.
exact_ablation: Add only a categorical tab-hour cross feature to the existing five-field additive scorer; retain all existing fields, RankNet loss, optimizer, sampling, split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive change, approximately 0 to +0.005, if the cross feature distinguishes within-user candidate ordering by surface and time.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.006, with possible benefit in weak context slices but limited global coverage per cross value.

text: Train the current RankNet scorer with group-stratified minibatches that deliberately preserve a controlled mixture of mixed-label, zero-positive, and all-positive groups.
rationale: The current training code keeps groups intact but does not explicitly control their label-stratum mixture; a stratified sampler can reduce optimization variance and prevent mixed groups from dominating the pairwise objective.
exact_ablation: Change only the train-group sampling policy to a fixed group-count mixture of 60% mixed, 20% zero-positive, and 20% all-positive groups, emitting complete groups; retain RankNet, features, model, optimizer, batch row budget, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive change, approximately 0 to +0.005, if more stable exposure to valid pair groups improves generalization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.005, because better optimization may help top ranks but homogeneous groups provide no direct pairwise signal.

text: Use a hybrid loss that combines within-user RankNet with a small pointwise BCE anchor over the same displayed impressions.
rationale: Experiment 2 improved neither official metric over experiment 1, and pure pairwise training may discard absolute propensity information needed for top-five selection; a small BCE anchor tests whether that trade-off is harmful.
exact_ablation: Add only a pointwise BCE term with fixed weight 0.10 to the existing within-user RankNet loss; retain features, architecture, optimizer, group sampling, split, and early stopping.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.005, if the anchor stabilizes score learning without overwhelming pairwise ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive change, approximately 0 to +0.006, if absolute relevance calibration helps identify top candidates among close pairwise scores.

text: Remove weekday while retaining tab and hour to test whether the observed context gain comes from intraday and surface effects rather than a weak calendar term.
rationale: The full request-context screen is positive but unstable by day, and experiment 2 shows large hour and tab variation; isolating weekday removal is a clean diagnostic ablation that may reduce noise and overfitting.
exact_ablation: Remove only the weekday input from the current user/video/tab/hour/weekday scorer; retain tab, hour, model, BCE training, optimizer, split, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.002 to +0.003, if weekday contributes little within-user discrimination and adds unstable parameters.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small negative change, approximately -0.003 to +0.002, because removing a weak field is unlikely to improve top-five ordering unless it reduces noise.

text: Replace the full request-context family with tab alone, testing whether the strongest surface-specific weakness can be addressed without the noisier hour and weekday terms.
rationale: Tab slices are dramatically weaker than the aggregate score, while the screen only establishes a bundled context gain; this isolates the surface signal and reduces context dimensionality for a clean confirmation.
exact_ablation: Keep only tab from the request-context family and remove hour and weekday; retain user/video IDs, additive architecture, BCE, optimizer, sampling, split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small negative or flat change, approximately -0.004 to +0.002, because hour contributed potentially useful variation and tab alone may not resolve weak surfaces.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small negative or flat change, approximately -0.005 to +0.002, with downside if hour helps rank candidates within a surface.

text: Train the current scorer with a top-one listwise loss over intact groups while retaining a small pointwise BCE anchor, rather than using pairwise RankNet.
rationale: This combines direct top-of-list competition with a calibration anchor and targets the observed mismatch between acceptable aggregate ordering and severe top-five failures in weak tabs.
exact_ablation: Replace RankNet with mixed-group ListNet plus a fixed 0.10-weight pointwise BCE anchor; retain the same scorer, features, optimizer, complete-group batching, split, and early stopping.

expected_effect.GAUC: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.005, because the BCE anchor may preserve broad ordering while ListNet changes within-group emphasis.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Moderate positive potential, approximately +0.001 to +0.010, if top-five failures arise from the pairwise loss treating all valid pairs too uniformly.

text: Add a shared-trunk auxiliary head for an impression-level engagement behavior while using only the long-view head for ranking.
rationale: Long-view is sparse and experiment 1 shows a measurable context-driven baseline; auxiliary supervision could shape representations without changing serving features, provided auxiliary labels use the same mature impression rows and are not fed as inputs.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one auxiliary engagement prediction head and a fixed 0.10-weight auxiliary BCE term to the existing pointwise model; retain long-view as the serving score, current features, optimizer, split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or negative change, approximately -0.003 to +0.006, because shared supervision may improve sparse representation learning but can cause negative transfer.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive, flat, or negative change, approximately -0.004 to +0.006, depending on whether the auxiliary behavior aligns with top-five long-view relevance.
